# Explainable ENSO skill from climate-mode memory

Skilful ENSO forecasts past about one year remain difficult, and even strong AI scores are hard to attach to named physical processes [ENSO skill beyond one year remains hard](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-84df85b1aaff761d) [AI skill is not yet process-linked](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-907a2d4c36298427). This paper’s move is an **extended nonlinear recharge oscillator (XRO)**: a low-order ENSO recharge–discharge core coupled to seasonally modulated autoregressive models of eight remote climate modes (NPMM, SPMM, IOB, IOD, SIOD, TNA, ATL3, SASD), so long-lead skill can be attributed to those modes’ initial conditions, memory, and coupling [XRO for explainable 16–18-month forecasts](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-946a0ca6864a96fb).

## How XRO isolates explainable skill

ENSO is represented by Niño3.4 SST and equatorial Pacific warm-water volume (WWV); the remote modes enter as SST indices. The joint tendency is driven by a seasonally modulated linear operator

$$\mathbf{L}=\begin{pmatrix}\mathbf{L}_{\mathrm{ENSO}}&\mathbf{C}_1\\\mathbf{C}_2&\mathbf{L}_M\end{pmatrix},$$

plus quadratic nonlinearities for ENSO/IOD asymmetry and red-noise forcing (Eqs. 1–5). Here $\mathbf{L}_{\mathrm{ENSO}}$ is ENSO recharge–discharge dynamics, $\mathbf{L}_M$ the remote-mode block, $\mathbf{C}_1$ inbound remote feedbacks onto ENSO, and $\mathbf{C}_2$ ENSO teleconnections outward [XRO state equation](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-c00af975fc62187d) [L block matrix definition](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-c82a14c19f35aff5). A tropical-Pacific-only **nRO** is the no-remote-coupling baseline [nRO isolates tropical-Pacific dynamics](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-5cc545cd52b7a934).

A 43,000-year stochastically forced run reproduces observed Niño3.4 seasonality, skewness, spectrum, WWV lead, and lead–lag links to the remote modes (Figure 2, left and middle panels) [XRO reproduces ENSO traits and mode links](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-10a9d4b71d7b5f2c). Out-of-sample reforecasts (fit 1950–1999, verify 2002–2022) show XRO beating the IRI dynamical multi-model mean beyond about 9 months and matching top AI skill; control reforecasts for 1979–2022 keep Niño3.4 correlation above 0.5 at an 18-month lead and weaken the spring predictability barrier that limits the nRO (Figure 2, right-hand skill panels) [Out-of-sample XRO matches AI, beats IRI dynamical means](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-fe9567d9cc7f8079) [Control XRO ACC > 0.5 at 18 months](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-6a428d85cf5026fb) [XRO weakens the spring predictability barrier](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-1a6b71069a3ada6b) [Figure 2 caption: skilful to 16–18 months](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-25b3ee5c427c07c6).

![Figure 2 · Source figure](xro-report-assets/fig-2.webp)

Fig. 2|Superior efficacy of the XRO in simulating and reforecasting ENSO. a-c, Seasonally varying standard deviation (a), skewness (b) and power spectrum (c) of Niño3.4 using ORAS5 (black) and the XRO stochastic simulation (red). d-I, Monthly cross-correlations between Niño3.4 and different indices: WWV (d), NPMM (e), SPMM (f), IOB (g), IOD (h), SIOD (i), TNA (j), ATL3 (k) and SASD (I). Dashed grey curves show the autocorrelation of Niño3.4 and vertical blue dashed lines denote lead times of 6 (WWV), 6 (NPMM), 4 (SPMM), 12 (IOB), 14 (IOD), 10 (SIOD), 9 (TNA), 6 (ATL3) and 9 (SASD) months. Abscissas indicate lead time in months (negative values representing Niño3.4 lag). Red shading indicates the 10–90% ensemble spread of simulated 43 year segments, obtained from splitting a 43,000 year XRO simulation into 1,000 non- overlapping parts. m, All-months correlation skill of 3 month running mean Niño3.4 as a function of forecast lead for forecasts verified on 2002-2022 for the out-of-sample nRO (magenta) and XRO (red) fitted on 1950-1999, the AI model (blue), the XRO control fitted on 1979-2022 (black) and IRI operational
models, the ensemble mean of dynamical models (dark purple curve) and ensemble mean of statistical models (dark cvan curve). n, Same as m, but for Niño3.4 forecast skills for nRO (magenta) and XRO (red) control forecasts, AI model forecasts (blue), and NMME dynamical model forecasts (multi-model ensemble mean in black, ensemble means fromindividual models in other colours). Validation period is 1979-2022 except for the AI and NMME models (period indicated in the legend). o,p, Correlation skill of nRO (o) and XRO (p) Niño3.4 forecasts as a function ofinitialization month (ordinate) and target month (abscissa; superscripts 0,1 and 2 denote the current and subsequent years, respectively). Hatching highlights forecasts with a correlation less than 0.5. The dashed vertical blue lines denote the SPB. The XRO accurately simulates the fundamental observed ENSO characteristics, its lead-lag relationships with other climate modes and provides skilful forecasts at lead times up to 16-18 months. [Figure 2 source](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-4618c6e790f9e57e)

## What the uninitialized experiments show

Among uninitialized, decoupled, and observation-relaxation basin tests, only **uninitialized** runs give nearly additive basin skill shares; decoupling overestimates each basin because of indirect cross-basin pathways (Figure 3; Extended Data Figure 3) [Only uninitialized tests fairly quantify additive basin skill](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-aa6c31c7c00d457a) [Decoupling overestimates basin shares](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-12de87edaf95e2e2). The skill gain over nRO comes mainly from remote-mode **initial-condition memory**, not from ENSO-triggered coupled feedbacks alone [Skill gains are mainly remote IC memory](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-8ede9720eaa04c00). Seasonally, ExPO (especially NPMM) helps boreal-winter targets, IO (especially IOD) helps late-year starts, and AO (TNA/SASD) helps winter–spring starts; peak-phase composites credit NPMM, IOD, and TNA as the main extra amplitude sources [ExPO, IO, and AO add seasonal skill](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-f1eb75d6da1f2151) [NPMM, IOD, and TNA dominate extra amplitude](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-b8e905b6b5550174) [Figure 3 caption: seasonal basin contributions](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-17da3a4a01cdc87e).

![Figure 3 · Source figure](xro-report-assets/fig-3.webp)

Fig. 3|Quantifying theincreased ENSO forecast skills from the coupled influences outside equatorialPacific during1979-2022. a, The all-months correlation skill of the 3 month running mean Niño3.4 index as a function of the forecast lead month in the control experiment (XRO, black line), the uninitialized \mathsf { E x P O } + \mathsf { I O } + \mathsf { A O } experiment ( U _ { \tt E x P O + l O + A O } , removinginitial conditions of other basins; red line), the decoupled \mathsf { E x P O } + \mathsf { I O } + \mathsf { A O } experiment ( D _ { \tt E x P O + l O + A O } , removing the coupling of ENSO with other basins; blue line) and the relaxing Ex \mathsf { P O } + \mathsf { I O } + \mathsf { A O } to observations experiment ( R _ { \tt E x P O + l O + A O } , addingperfect 'future' information of other basins in a hindcast case; magenta line). b-d, The skill difference of the Niño3.4 index as a function of initial time and target
month between XRO and D _ { \mathsf { E x P 0 + 1 0 + A 0 } } ( \mathbf { b } ) ,between XRO and U _ { \scriptscriptstyle \mathrm { E x P O + 1 0 + A O } } ( \mathbf { c } ) and between U _ { \mathrm { E x P O + 1 0 + A 0 } } { \bf a n d } D _ { \mathrm { E x P O + 1 0 + A 0 } } ( { \bf d } ) . { \bf e - g } Same as d, but for the difference between control and the uninitialized ExPO (e), IO (f) and AO (g) experiments. Hatching indicates that the correlation difference is significant at a 90% confidencelevelusingthetwo-tailed Fisher z-transformationtest.The sensitivity experiments demonstrate the importance of the extratropical Pacific, IO and AO in enhancing ENSO forecast skill, with distinct seasonal dependence. The interbasin memory sustains ENSO forecast skill beyond the SPB with the IO and AO contributing skill in boreal summer and the ExPO in boreal winter. [Figure 3 source](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-1165ede5cf609e6c)

Training XRO on 91 CMIP historical runs yields lower, more spread-out Niño3.4 skill than observation-trained XRO. Swapping in observed $\mathbf{L}_{\mathrm{ENSO}}$ helps most at long leads; correcting inbound $\mathbf{C}_1$ helps intermediate leads; correcting outbound $\mathbf{C}_2$ helps remote modes more than Niño3.4 [CMIP-trained XROm skill lags observations](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-d098a1befc603a0f) [Fixing ENSO dynamics and inbound feedbacks beats outbound teleconnections](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-f9dc3fc8e63c2c79).

## Boundaries to keep in view

XRO’s advantage over nRO is attributed to remote-mode initial conditions, seasonally modulated memory, and teleconnections under an unbiased operator—not to a free-running CGCM [Models need recharge dynamics plus remote ICs, memory, and teleconnections](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-c346a3fb7b368e83). Fits use about 40–50 years for 515 free parameters; multiplicative state-dependent noise is acknowledged but not well constrained by record length [515 parameters need ~40–50 years](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-db3fe7c6893dfe64) [State-dependent noise magnitude is hard to estimate](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-8df3e537615d1d5f). Satellite-era control skill and ORAS5-centred fits are the main showcase; XRO2 pantropical/type extensions are supportive, not the primary proof. Higher-frequency MJO–WWB coupling and decadal change pathways are stated outlook, not demonstrated here [Outlook: MJO–WWB and decadal pathways](thinkreader://paper/paper-c28b83a93504457a?evidence=ev-e65b87702222f223).
